liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Fire On The Mountain** (2 reviews): Reviewer describes a smoldering Cold Rain and Snow into Fire, reminiscent of an early-eighties show; Reviewer names Fire as the high point of the show [16][18]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Tennessee Jed, along with Dupree's, as a great rendition in a short first set [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Phil's Spacey Intro/Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **Phil Welcomes America,Welcomes Austin Texas, Welcomes Everyone To Farm Aid TV!**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **Thank You All And Have A Safe And Sane Fourth!**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Encore Break (Tape Paused Between) [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1986-07-04.111541.Nak300CP4.Floater.Keo.Flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 112 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1986-07-04.145496.fob.senn441.akerman.noel.t-flac16**: audience recording; 19 songs; 110 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [3]
- **gd1986-07-04.sbd.miller.89997.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 114 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [4]
- **gd1986-07-04.143038.FOB.Senn441.Akerman.Noel.t-flac2496**: audience recording; 18 songs; 110 min [8]
- **gd86-07-04.senn.eD.12930.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 103 min; rated 3.42/5 by 24 [14]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says this front-of-board recording is the better of two, with a meaty texture and prominent Phil; Reviewer says the 421 microphones give better bass response, with lots of Phil [16][18]

## Around the show

- Reviewer recalls spoken-word, rap-style music played during the break, possibly Burroughs or Ginsberg [17]
- Reviewer says the day was hot, but Dylan, not in best form, and Petty's mixed fans were noticeable on the floor [19]
- Reviewer met Richard Manuel's wife on the way from Poughkeepsie to Buffalo; she showed photo albums [19]
- Reviewer says many Tom Petty fans in the crowd resembled Petty, and it was a weird show to take acid at [21]
- Reviewer left before Petty finished, finding Rich Stadium too tiring while heavily intoxicated [23]
- Reviewer and companion left before Petty came on after she got sick; they barely remember Dylan [25]
- Reviewer recalls a beautiful day with no rain, contradicting other accounts [27]
- Reviewer says the Dead's set was short because Petty and Dylan with Petty played two opening sets, not because of Jerry [27]
- Reviewer finds Jerry sounds better than remembered, though not the most energetic show they saw [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1986-07-04.111541.Nak300CP4.Floater.Keo.Flac2496**: taped by Keo; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Nakamichi CM300/CP4 Shotguns>DBX Reduction>Sony D5 Tapes:Maxell XLII-S 90,90 Taper:Floater,Transfer by Keo Transfer with Nakamichi MR-1>Korg… [1]. Also: Source tapes came from Floater; first-set tape is paused between songs, cutting some audience sound [1]
- **gd1986-07-04.145496.fob.senn441.akerman.noel.t-flac16**: taped by Ray Ackerman; source: Recording & Transfer by Ray Ackerman; Sennheiser 441 > Sony D5 > Master Audience Cassettes (FOB) [3]. Also: Edited and mastered by Joe Noel from Ray's Sennheiser 441 tape, patched with Nakamichi CM300/CP4 source, with crossfaded first-set pauses [3]
- **gd1986-07-04.sbd.miller.89997.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette -> Dat (48k) D [4]. Also: Front-of-board Sennheiser 421 to cassette master, then DAT, then CD; part of show broadcast live on Farm Aid [4]
- **gd1986-07-04.143038.FOB.Senn441.Akerman.Noel.t-flac2496**: taped by Ray Akerman; transferred by Joe Noel; source: Recording & Transfer by Ray Ackerman; Sennheiser 441 > Sony D5 > Master Audience Cassettes (FOB); Transfer; Master Cassettes (Nakamichi 700 MKii) > Oade… [8]. Also: Taped by Ray on Sennheiser 441s; set one from Floater and Keo's Nakamichi source, set two patched by Don Crandel [8]
- **gd86-07-04.senn.eD.12930.sbeok.shnf**: source: FOB-AUD>MC>DAT>CDR [14]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Pete Mason: [Truckin’ off to Buffalo: The Grateful Dead open for Bob Dylan and Tom Petty at Rich Stadium on July 4, 1986](https://nysmusic.com/2020/07/04/truckin-off-to-buffalo-34-years-ago-the-grateful-dead-open-for-bob-dylan-and-tom-petty-at-rich-stadium/) [29]
- Fan art by Pete Mason: [Truckin’ off to Buffalo: The Grateful Dead open for Bob Dylan and Tom Petty at Rich Stadium on July 4, 1986](https://nysmusic.com/2020/07/04/truckin-off-to-buffalo-34-years-ago-the-grateful-dead-open-for-bob-dylan-and-tom-petty-at-rich-stadium/) [30]
- Poster by Ron Delany Grateful Dead: [1986-07-04 Rich Stadium, Buffalo, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1986-07-04-rich-stadium-buffalo-ny-usa/) [31]

claims.text: Reviewer says this front-of-board recording is the better of two, with a meaty texture and prominent Phil
Reviewer singles out Tennessee Jed, along with Dupree's, as a great rendition in a short first set
Reviewer describes a smoldering Cold Rain and Snow into Fire, reminiscent of an early-eighties show
Reviewer recalls spoken-word, rap-style music played during the break, possibly Burroughs or Ginsberg
Reviewer says the 421 microphones give better bass response, with lots of Phil
Reviewer names Fire as the high point of the show
Reviewer says the day was hot, but Dylan, not in best form, and Petty's mixed fans were noticeable on the floor
Reviewer met Richard Manuel's wife on the way from Poughkeepsie to Buffalo; she showed photo albums
Reviewer says many Tom Petty fans in the crowd resembled Petty, and it was a weird show to take acid at
Reviewer left before Petty finished, finding Rich Stadium too tiring while heavily intoxicated
Reviewer finds Jerry sounds better than remembered, though not the most energetic show they saw
Reviewer and companion left before Petty came on after she got sick; they barely remember Dylan
Reviewer recalls a beautiful day with no rain, contradicting other accounts
Reviewer says the Dead's set was short because Petty and Dylan with Petty played two opening sets, not because of Jerry
Dylan and Petty with the Heartbreakers opened; Samson, The Wheel and I Need A Miracle were televised for Farm Aid
Source tapes came from Floater; first-set tape is paused between songs, cutting some audience sound
Edited and mastered by Joe Noel from Ray's Sennheiser 441 tape, patched with Nakamichi CM300/CP4 source, with crossfaded first-set pauses
The band is stalling for time at the onset; Dylan and Petty opened, and the show was broadcast via satellite
Taped by Ray on Sennheiser 441s; set one from Floater and Keo's Nakamichi source, set two patched by Don Crandel
Front-of-board Sennheiser 421 to cassette master, then DAT, then CD; part of show broadcast live on Farm Aid
